input.rationale: Of the three compositions measured, index 13 (Bi0.11 Cu0.42 V0.48) had the highest photocurrent at 1.05e-6 A. Its XRD shows monoclinic BiVO4 peaks (Q≈1.34, 2.03, 2.66) plus extra peaks at Q≈1.575 and 1.93, which likely come from a Cu vanadate (Cu:V near 1:1). Adding Cu vanadate to BiVO4 may improve visible light absorption at 2.4 eV compared with nearly pure BiVO4.

rejected.reason: Nearly single-phase BiVO4 with Cu (Bi:V about 1:1). Photocurrent was only 4.0e-7 A. BiVO4's band gap is close to the 2.4 eV illumination, so it absorbs weakly.

At the more Cu-rich composition (Cu:V about 1.4), XRD shows a different Cu vanadate phase (new peaks at Q≈0.97, 1.61, 1.74). Photocurrent dropped to 6.2e-7 A, so going further toward Cu made it worse.
Likely dominated by CuO and CuBi2O4, which are p-type photocathode materials and unlikely to work as photoanodes. Not measured.

content.text:
I submitted **index 13** (Bi 0.11, Cu 0.42, V 0.48). It had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, at 1.05 µA. I used all 3 merit measurements and 4 of the 5 XRD scans, so 134 of the 137 compositions were never measured. I can't tell how close index 13 is to the best in the library.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | What the XRD showed | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 53 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | Nearly pure BiVO4 | 0.40 µA |
| **13** | 0.11 / 0.42 / 0.48 | BiVO4 plus extra peaks, probably a copper vanadate | **1.05 µA** |
| 69 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 | BiVO4 plus a different set of extra peaks | 0.62 µA |

- **Why index 13 may do better:** BiVO4 absorbs weakly at the 2.4 eV illumination because its band gap is close to that energy. Mixing in a copper vanadate, which has a smaller gap, likely helps it absorb more light.
- **Too much copper hurt:** moving on to the more Cu-rich index 69 lowered the photocurrent. The best point is probably somewhere near Cu 0.40–0.45 and V around 0.5.
- **Untested neighbours:** nearby compositions such as indices 52, 22, 26 and 68 might beat index 13, but I had no measurements left to check them.
- **Cu-rich, low-V half of the library (indices 71–136):** I skipped it entirely. It is probably dominated by CuO and CuBi2O4, which normally behave as photocathodes rather than photoanodes. That is based on known chemistry, not on any measurement here.

The phase labels are my reading of the peak positions. Only the BiVO4 match is solid; I didn't identify the extra phases exactly.
